implementation.receiver: ECX, aliased to a local at 0x006a1519 (MOV ESI,ECX) and never rewritten before 0x006a152d

observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The receiver arrives in ECX and is copied to ESI at 0x006a1519 (MOV ESI,ECX); the machine-derived receiver record names register ECX, shape R-ALIAS, offsets [0], bounds_only true. The single ordinary stack dword is read at 0x006a1512 as [ESP + 0xc], which after the two preceding pushes is entry_ESP+0x4, and it is never written. The terminator RET 0x4 at 0x006a1533 pops four bytes, so the callee owns the cleanup; that excludes cdecl and fastcall, and ECX carrying the receiver makes __thiscall the only consistent convention. categories.abi_derived.conventions.confidence is INFERRED, not OBSERVED.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: unclassified_in_EAX -- the machine-derived record classes the EAX left behind as aggregate_unknown with type null; the last write to EAX is the result of the register-indirect CALL at 0x006a152f and the body applies no further operation to it
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x006a152f CALL EAX is the final EAX write; 0x006a1531 POP EDI, 0x006a1532 POP ESI and 0x006a1533 RET 0x4 follow without touching it. The reconstructed body returns the value of the second transfer, which is the only reading consistent with the listing. Ghidra's live record types the same function void (ghidra_function.return_type, return_type_resolved true); that is a decompiler judgement, not a machine ABI record, and the two are reported side by side rather than merged.
observed_original_abi.variadic: no evidence of varargs; the terminator pops exactly one dword
observed_original_abi.ghidra_convention_note: The live decompilation header reads 'WARNING: Unknown calling convention'; categories.abi_derived.cross_validation records ghidra=no_information and ghidra_parameter_count=2, so the convention here is the derived one, not a cross-validated one.

mechanics.body_shape: straight-line prologue, one null test, two register-indirect transfers, epilogue
mechanics.prologue: 0x006a1510 PUSH ESI; 0x006a1511 PUSH EDI. No frame pointer, no stack allocation: the two pushes are the whole frame, and they exist to preserve ESI/EDI, not to build a frame.
mechanics.argument_load: 0x006a1512 MOV EDI,dword ptr [ESP + 0xc] -- the single stack argument, hoisted into EDI and used twice: once as the base of the +0x30 read and once as the stack argument of the second transfer.
mechanics.receiver_alias: 0x006a1519 MOV ESI,ECX -- ESI carries the receiver for the rest of the body. Because the alias is a different register from ECX, a literal scan of the listing for ECX operands finds no displacement at all; the only receiver displacement the machine record enumerates is 0.
mechanics.word_read_0x30: 0x006a1516 MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDI + 0x30] -- one word out of the argument object. No record names the member; the reconstruction calls it a plain word and passes it on unchanged.
mechanics.null_test: 0x006a151b TEST EAX,EAX with 0x006a151d JZ 0x006a1527 -- a null word skips the first transfer only. The second transfer runs on both paths, and the branch target is inside this body.
mechanics.table_load: 0x006a151f MOV EDX,dword ptr [ESI] and 0x006a1527 MOV EDX,dword ptr [ESI] -- the table word at displacement 0, loaded twice, once per path. The shape is a vtable pointer; no record types it, so the reconstruction reads it as an opaque table word.
mechanics.first_transfer: 0x006a1521 PUSH EAX (the +0x30 word), 0x006a1522 MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDX + 0x38], 0x006a1525 CALL EAX. ECX is untouched, so the callee's receiver is this function's receiver. Its result is dead: 0x006a1529 overwrites EAX.
mechanics.second_transfer: 0x006a152c PUSH EDI (the argument), 0x006a152d MOV ECX,ESI (the receiver alias becomes the callee's ECX), 0x006a1529 MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDX + 0x30], 0x006a152f CALL EAX. Its result is the body's return value.
mechanics.direct_call_targets: none: the listing holds no CALL or JMP immediate, and the xref export records no call edge out of this function
mechanics.data_segment_addresses: none in the listing and none in the reconstruction
mechanics.callee_cleanup_inference: INFERENCE, not observation: the frame is balanced at 0x006a1531/0x006a1532 with no ADD ESP after either CALL, so each of the two slot callees must have popped the single word it was handed. This is why the two slot function-pointer types are declared __thiscall with one stack argument; if a slot target turns out to clean up in cdecl, those two types are what changes.
mechanics.vtable_associations: categories.function_identity lists vtable:0x01408820 and vtable:0x01408870, and ghidra_function.xrefs are the two table slots 0x01408858 and 0x014088a8. No 0x01xxxxxx address is named in the reconstruction source: the association is a classifier claim, and dependencies.vtable_reference_count for this record is 0.
mechanics.stack_displacement_note: The +0x30 word is read from the argument object in EDI, not from the receiver, so it is not a receiver displacement and is not constrained by the receiver record's bounds (offsets [0], bounds_only true).

return_semantics.observation: The word is the return value of the register-indirect transfer at 0x006a152f and is not operated on before RET 0x4.
return_semantics.ownership: No reference acquisition, release or copy happens in this body; ownership of the value is not established here.
return_semantics.disagreement: categories.abi_derived.value.return is {register EAX, register_class aggregate_unknown, type null, void_possible false} -- and void_possible is false only because the inference raises that flag solely when EAX is never written and no call can clobber it (abi_infer RT3), which this body does not satisfy. Ghidra types the function void. The reconstruction follows the machine record and names the return type unclassified_in_EAX; adopting void instead is a one-token change to the declaration and is an open question, not a settled fact.
return_semantics.lifetime: Nothing in this body establishes how long the returned word stays valid; the two xrefs are table slots, so the callers are the receiver's own table users and are not identified.

evidence.decompiler_caveat: The decompiled C reads the word out of this->mpParent and dispatches on in_ECX, i.e. it mixes the receiver and the argument; the listing shows the +0x30 read is on EDI (the argument) and both slots are read through ESI (the receiver alias). unresolved_questions: What does the table word at displacement 0x38 hold? It is read at 0x006a1522 and called at 0x006a1525 with this function's receiver in ECX and the +0x30 word of the argument as its single stack argument. No record in this repository names that target, and the two vtable associations of the function (0x01408820, 0x01408870) are classifier claims rather than slot identities.

What does the table word at displacement 0x30 hold? It is read at 0x006a1529 and called at 0x006a152f with the receiver in ECX and the stack argument as its single stack argument, and its result is what this body returns. The SDK name makes a void mutator plausible, which is also what the Ghidra decompilation asserts, but no record identifies the slot.

What is the +0x30 word of the argument object? The listing reads it once, tests it for null, and passes it as a stack argument. It is read from the argument, not from the receiver, so the receiver record does not cover it and no record names it; the decompiler's mpParent is one decompiler's guess and is not adopted.

Do the two slot callees really clean up their stack argument? Callee cleanup is inferred from a balanced frame with no ADD ESP; no callee is identified, so the __thiscall shape of the two slot function-pointer types is an inference that a target resolution would confirm or refute.

Is the return type void or an unclassified word? The machine-derived record declines to classify it (register_class aggregate_unknown, type null) while Ghidra types it void. The reconstruction follows the machine record's own classification string and reports the disagreement rather than resolving it.

The machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only and enumerates displacement 0 and nothing else, while a literal scan of the listing for ECX operands finds no displacement at all, because the body aliases the receiver into ESI at 0x006a1519 and reads it only as [ESI]. The record and the body therefore agree on the single receiver word this body touches, but that agreement is not evidence that 0x0 is the receiver's only word: a bounds_only record states where the body was seen reaching and is not an enumeration of the object, so it can neither confirm nor refute any receiver word this body happens not to touch. No record in this repository gives the receiver's layout.
